articles.title: Extension Update Authority Decides What Runs on the Endpoint. Uninstalling Doesn't Undo It.
articles.summary:
Extension update authority is the decision about who can change code on an engineering endpoint without an acquisition event the organization controls. On October 29, 2026, that decision was tested in the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace. According to Cursor, a maliciously modified Anthropic.claude-code extension, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 in Windows and macOS packages, was available between about 2:27am and 1:35pm PT, roughly eleven hours. Cursor states that Anthropic did not develop the malicious versions.

articles.title: Varlock Releases Bumpy: A File-Based Versioning Alternative to Changesets
articles.summary: Bumpy is an MIT-licensed, TypeScript tool for version management and changelogs in monorepos. It follows the changesets workflow, using markdown bump files, and adds support for workspace and catalog protocols, custom publish commands, and branch-based prereleases. Changesets v3, released in August 2026, closed many earlier gaps, though differences remain. By Daniel Curtis

articles.title: 6 AI Coding Tips That Sound Wrong (But Actually Work)
articles.summary:
Most advice regarding coding with AI optimizes for the first demo. 

Write clearer prompts. Generate more code. Iterate fast. Those tips now feel like bottom-of-the-barrel advice. 

The tips that have produced features I can still open and trust weeks later do the opposite: they constrain the agent earlier, force smaller outputs, and treat the natural-language instructions as part of the codebase.

articles.summary: Meta's Muse agents continue to get new features and integrations. Spaces promises to be a new way to interact with the AI helpers.

articles.title: How Grab Improved Mobile App Stability by Safely Handling Surge in AI-Generated Code Changes
articles.summary: The growing adoption of AI coding assistants has accelerated development and increased the volume of code changes per release, bringing more opportunities for defects and crashes, says Grab. To address these challenges, they implemented a layered defense strategy to prevent, detect, and contain crashes throughout the development and release lifecycle. By Sergio De Simone

articles.title: Beyond code generation: A developer’s guide to agentic engineering
articles.summary:
Writing code got faster. The work around it didn't. See how you can plan, write code, review changes, and investigate production issues with GitHub Copilot, and what work still needs your judgment.
The post Beyond code generation: A developer’s guide to agentic engineering appeared first on The GitHub Blog.

articles.title: Edera's Object Capability Bounded Authority Promises to Isolate Credentials From AI Agent Workloads
articles.summary: Edera announced Object Capability Bounded Authority, a security model that separates an AI agent's or MCP server's required authority from the credentials behind it. Hypervisor-enforced capabilities limit agents to specific actions without storing secrets in the workload. Initial releases cover scoped command execution and workload identity; credential-brokered API access will follow. By Olimpiu Pop

articles.title: Yelp Combines Native and Server-Driven UI for Its AI Assistant
articles.summary: Yelp combines native mobile controls with server-driven conversation rendering in its AI Assistant using the CHAOS framework. The architecture separates view configuration from conversation data, supports backend-driven chat interactions, and enables faster UI updates without new app releases. Yelp also discusses cross-platform challenges and reuse for its Biz Ask Anything pilot. By Leela Kumili

articles.title: GitLab 19.5 Makes Agentic Development a Governed Part of the DevOps Platform
articles.summary: GitLab 19.5, released on October 15, puts agentic software development and governance at the centre of the platform, making its GitLab MCP server generally available while expanding how external AI agents can interact with GitLab. By Craig Risi

articles.title: Higgs Realtime Duplex: a 45B MoE full-duplex model that listens, watches and talks at once, and thinks, calls tools and delegates in the background [N]
articles.summary: Disclosure: I'm at Boson AI and this is our release. Not open weights; the Duplex API has a waitlist, and the previous turn-based Higgs Realtime is available now. Most voice models are still turn-based: listen, wait for end of turn, think, speak. Duplex runs all streams at once and keeps working in the background while it talks. Streams. articles.summary: Physicl is trying to solve the sim-to-real gap with a pipeline originally built to market goods online.

articles.title: TypeScript 7.1 Beta: Restores the Compiler API and Makes Vue and Svelte First-Class
articles.summary: TypeScript 7.1 Beta, announced October 20, 2026, restores the compiler API removed in 7.0, now split into separate entry points. It adds content mappers, letting tools like Vue check non-standard files. One Vue project's type checks fell from 14.19 to 3.10 seconds. An editor issue remains open, and teams may need TypeScript 6 alongside 7. By Daniel Curtis

articles.summary:
Three Python classes, an OpenRouter key, and gpt-4.1-mini give the agent a calculator, a stub web search, and conversation recall that survives restarts.
The post Give Your Python AI Agent Persistent Memory with One JSON File appeared first on Towards Data Science.

articles.title: AWS Ships Continuum for Code Vulnerabilities
articles.summary: AWS has made Continuum for code vulnerabilities generally available in two regions. The service proves exploitability by running real exploits in a sandbox, then opens fixes as pull requests. Published pricing charges per finding processed as well as per line of code, and practitioners are asking what would justify letting it merge fixes on its own. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
